Charles Schwab stock faces jobs data after record quarter
sum: U.S. labor-market figures will set the main agenda for Charles Schwab investors next week. The October Employment Situation report is scheduled for Friday, November 6, at 8:30 a.m. Eastern Time, according to InvestingLive.

The calendar cited by the market publication calls for nonfarm payrolls to rise by 63,000, compared with 29,000 previously. The unemployment rate is expected to remain at 4.2%, while average hourly earnings are forecast to increase 0.3% month over month after 0.1% previously. The combination could influence expectations for interest rates and the trading environment for financial firms.

Charles Schwab entered the week with strong operating momentum. In its October 15 release, the company reported third-quarter net revenue of 7.171 billion U.S. dollars, up 17% from a year earlier. GAAP diluted earnings per share reached 1.62 U.S. dollars, while adjusted diluted earnings per share came to 1.69 U.S. dollars after 151 million U.S. dollars of pretax transaction-related costs.

Client activity also strengthened. Total client assets reached 13.33 trillion U.S. dollars at the end of September, and daily average trading volume increased 44% year over year to 10.7 million trades. Schwab said core net new assets totaled 190.4 billion U.S. dollars during the quarter.

For Schwab, the jobs report matters through both market activity and monetary policy expectations. A resilient labor market could support trading engagement, while wage pressure may keep attention on the interest-rate outlook. Softer hiring could raise growth concerns, even if it increases expectations for easier policy.

Why Charles Schwab Stock Bumped Almost 4% Higher on Monday
sum: We can't say that Charles Schwab's (NYSE: SCHW) proprietary equity index is as closely followed as, say, the S&P 500 index. But when the Schwab Trading Activity Index (STAX) rises notably, investors take notice. That was the dynamic behind the brokerage's nearly 4% price bump on Monday.

During that day's trading session, Schwab announced that its self-named index had risen to 59.12 in June, notably up from its May level of slightly over 55. That set a multi-year high, the company pointed out.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

This is indicative of more than just investor eagerness to own stock, at least according to STAX's owner. The veteran financial company claims that it's a unique behavioral index "that analyzes retail investor stock positions and trading activity from Schwab's millions of client accounts to illuminate what investors were actually doing and how they were positioned in the markets each month.

The company wrote that STAX's June performance was bolstered by bargain-hunting during market pullbacks. Schwab investors were net buyers of index and exchange-traded fund (ETF) options, while they also plowed into tech, communications, and consumer discretionary stocks. By age group, the STAX data showed that Generation X investors were particularly bullish in June.

We live in a world stuffed full of securities indexes, so I wouldn't add STAX to the list of essentials to monitor. That said, it is a multi-dimensional indicator that can be revealing of investor trends and habits, factors that always affect the market to some extent.
While I wouldn't buy, sell, or hold Schwab stock based on STAX's latest performance, I'm nevertheless encouraged to see that level of activity at the brokerage.

The Retail Trading Boom Is Back. Charles Schwab Is Quietly Cashing In.
sum: When investors look at the discount broker industry today, fresh new names like Robinhood (HOOD +3.21%) probably get more attention than established names like Charles Schwab (SCHW -1.18%). That likely makes sense, given that Charles Schwab is one of the oldest companies in the sector. However, it would be a mistake to dismiss this financial giant. Here's how Schwab is quietly benefiting from the retail trading boom that's underway.

In May 2026, Charles Schwab's customers held accounts worth $13.1 trillion dollars. That's a huge sum of money. For comparison's sake, Robinhood's total platform assets amounted to "only" $344 billion. That's not meant to be a put-down to Robinhood, which is a much younger company and has achieved impressive things in a very short period of time. It is meant to show just how large Charles Schwab's business really is. In fact, it was one of the companies that helped Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX +8.62%) go public.

It is easier to grow a small business, but that doesn't mean Charles Schwab isn't growing. The company's customer assets increased 27% year over year in May. That's a massive increase, helped along by rising stock prices and new accounts. According to the financial giant, "New brokerage accounts opened during the month totaled 461,000, an increase of 37% versus May 2025."

Every new account is a chance to earn more money from commissions, margin interest, and fee-generating services (from asset management services to the management fees earned from Schwab's own family of exchange-traded funds). On the trading front, the company hit a record daily average of 11.8 million trades in May. Margin loans, meanwhile, were up 38% from the end of 2025.

To be fair, Robinhood's growth opportunity is larger than Schwab's. But, as noted, it is easier to grow from a smaller base. There's a problem with that, as growth-enamored investors often push valuations to extreme levels. Notably, Robinhood's price-to-earnings ratio is 54x, while Schwab's is a far lower 19x.
Schwab is an industry giant that is quietly cashing in on the current trading boom. And you can buy it for less than half Robinhood's valuation.

The Charles Schwab Corporation’s stock has experienced notable upward momentum alongside significant intraday volatility, reflecting positive operational milestones, regulatory clarity, and constructive shifts in market sentiment. Financial institutions like Schwab have recently benefited from the broader industry-wide tailwinds provided by the Federal Reserve’s Comprehensive Capital Analysis and Review (CCAR) results.

The regulatory stress test results, which Schwab officially disclosed, confirm the company’s exceptionally robust capital position. Schwab reported a Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) ratio of 26.3%, far exceeding the regulatory minimum of 4.5% even when combined with its 2.5% stress capital buffer. This reassurance of balance sheet safety and capital adequacy has diminished risk premiums for the stock, allowing institutional and retail investors to trade with increased confidence.

Complementing this regulatory boost are the company’s stellar monthly operational metrics. Schwab’s core net new assets rose to record-breaking levels, driven by intense market participation and elevated trading volumes across its stock and exchange-traded fund platforms. The rapid onboarding of new brokerage accounts indicates that the firm continues to capture substantial market share, defying mature-growth expectations. Analyst optimism has concurrently gained traction, with several Wall Street firms upwardly revising their short-term earnings estimates and raising their price targets on expectations of persistent net interest margin expansion.

However, the intraday volatility accompanying this upward movement highlights persistent, underlying market tensions. General macroeconomic uncertainties ahead of critical employment data and comments from Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh have kept the broader financial sector on edge.
